sources.title: Self-driving startup Waabi makes global headlines after raising as much as US$1 billion

reading.body:
Waabi's patent record is about simulation and perception for autonomous driving, not about the compute or power behind it. Five granted patents since 2025 cover deferred neural lighting in augmented image generation, mixed reality simulation for autonomous systems, motion planning with implicit occupancy, real world object reconstruction, and trajectory value learning. The mix points to a company building its own synthetic training and planning stack rather than assembling one from vendors.

That matters for AI because autonomous trucking is a physical AI problem where the scarce input is validated driving experience, not model weights. Simulation is how a 2021 startup multiplies miles it has not driven. The two September 2026 grants on neural lighting and mixed reality simulation suggest the company treats rendering fidelity and world reconstruction as core research, which is consistent with its stated claim that one model serves both trucks and robotaxis.

The data does not show compute footprint, data center locations, power contracts, or fleet size, so it cannot support any claim about Waabi's energy or infrastructure constraints. It also records no products, lawsuits, or MCP servers, and the patent list is limited to grants matching the applicant phrase "waabi" in USPTO data since 2001. Nothing here establishes revenue, deployment scale, or whether the Volvo partnership has produced vehicles on the road.
